note: Quarters, eighths and sixteenths mixed (beat:5): a bar of each against the metronome, a change on every beat of one bar, then the bar the other way round and one of the player's own over drums. The old Stage choice of tempos is moves (50 to 70). The clap-along has one rhythm per round, so the mixed bars are counted aloud in the text over a backing-band click; a rhythm tool that plays a written mixed bar would carry them better.

exercise.title: Quarters, eighths and sixteenths in one bar
exercise.why: Quarters, eighths and sixteenths split the same beat into one, two and four, so as long as the numbers of your count stay on the click you can change from one to another on any beat.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Clap a bar of quarters, a bar of eighths and a bar of sixteenths, round and round, and count aloud: "1 2 3 4", then "1 & 2 &", then "1 e & a".
Listen for the numbers of your count: they land on the click in all three bars.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Clap one bar that goes quarter, two eighths, four sixteenths, quarter, and count it aloud: "1, 2 &, 3 e & a, 4".
Practice until you change from beat to beat without slowing down or rushing.
If the sixteenths run past the next click, say the count for a bar before you clap it.

Press Play below to start the drums. Clap the bar the other way round, four sixteenths, two eighths, quarter, quarter, counting "1 e & a, 2 &, 3, 4".
Then make up a bar of your own from the three, and clap it until it comes round the same every time.
If you lose the beat, press Click below to switch the metronome on and clap quarters for a bar.
